interpretation_limits: P1 is not a fixed task-to-agent organization: only its teaching relation is fixed; production is state-responsive.
P0 has no teaching actions in its policy action catalog; P1/P2 do. Physical budgets and accounting are shared, but action spaces differ by policy class.
Only stationary IID versus deterministic perfect alternation is contrasted; this does not estimate a demand-persistence response curve.
No Monte Carlo uncertainty estimate or population inference is supported.
This subcomparison cannot answer the HLS-P1 question about anticipatory development versus FIXED-OPT and REACTIVE.

model.demand_processes: existing S4 deterministic Markov alternation; stationary control uses existing IID StationaryTaskDemand at 0.5/0.5
model.observation_mode: imperfect, same coordinate-indexed observation seed across policies
model.reward: period CES production; separately reports functional success and deficit

policies.P0_PRODUCTION_ONLY: reactive current-view production rule; no teaching actions
policies.P1_FIXED_TEACHING: fixed A→B on skill y relation; production remains reactive
policies.P2_ADAPTIVE_TEACHING: existing relation-memory heuristic over A→B/y and B→A/x; not anticipatory

unavailable.FIXED_OPT: No globally optimized fixed organization is implemented in the N×K/MIS-v2 route.
unavailable.HLS_ANTICIPATORY: No exact anticipatory policy is implemented for the N×K/MIS-v2 transition. G0/RQ0 HLS exact uses a different A1 model.

randomness.common_random_numbers: same exogenous seed and frozen demand path within each scenario; same indexed information seed

scientific_question_coverage: Does not test FIXED-OPT or anticipatory optimization, nor vary demand persistence. Reports existing P0/P1/P2 behavior on the already-defined S4 deterministic alternating path.
title: Bounded existing-policy comparison on the S4 N×K/MIS-v2 diagnostic
